specs.title: Checkout discount
sources: Owner request: Add a discount to checkout
Binding: no provisional choices for prices
in_scope: Showing the discount on the checkout order summary
Recalculating the order total when a discount applies
non_goals: Discounts on pages other than checkout
Changes to the price list itself

criteria.text: Given a discount applies to the order, when the customer opens the order summary at checkout, then the discount is shown as its own line and the total reflects it.
criteria.check: Integration test of the checkout summary with a fixture discount.

criteria.text: Given a discount applies, when the order total is calculated, then the discount amount is the value decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Unit tests of the total calculation for each value decided in open question 1.

criteria.text: Given two discounts would both apply, when the order total is calculated, then the result follows the combination rule decided in open question 3.
criteria.check: Unit tests for each combination case decided in open question 3.

criteria.text: Given a discount the customer is not eligible for, when the customer applies it at checkout, then an error is shown and the total is unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative integration test; error text as decided in open question 2.

open_questions.question: What is the discount: a fixed amount, a percentage, or both, and what value?

options.changes: Criterion 2 takes a fixed value; no rounding rule needed.
Criterion 2 takes a percentage; a rounding rule is added.

open_questions.waiting_for: Owner (prices: no provisional choice allowed by the binding)

open_questions.question: Who receives the discount: all customers, or a defined group?

options.changes: Criterion 4 eligibility never fails.
An eligibility rule and its data source are added; criterion 4 is detailed.

open_questions.question: May this discount combine with other offers?

options.changes: Criterion 3 becomes a rejection of the second offer.
Criterion 3 gets the order rule and its rounding.

actions_now: Write the draft spec and put the discount size, eligibility and combination rules to the owner as open questions, without choosing; the binding forbids provisional price choices. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 wait for those answers; the checkout display work in criterion 1 does not depend on them and may proceed.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: CSV export version 1, approved (dl-014)
Implementer report: criterion 3 requires customer email; the reports API returns no emails; adding them is outside this line
in_scope: Unchanged from version 1, except criterion 3, which is suspended
non_goals: Adding customer email to the reports API, which belongs to another line

criteria.text: Suspended in version 2 pending open question 1: whether the export must include customer email. Criterion 3 of version 1 is not to be built until the owner decides.

open_questions.question: Must the CSV export include customer email, given the reports API does not provide it and adding it is a separate line that touches personal data?

options.option: Drop email from the export (criterion 3 removed)
options.changes: The export matches what the reports API returns; the owner approves the change to the approved version.

options.option: Keep email and add it in its own line that extends the reports API
options.changes: Criterion 3 stays; the export waits for the other line.

open_questions.waiting_for: Owner (personal data and the owner's approval of version 2)

versions: 2 (2026-11-27): criterion 3 suspended after the implementer's report; draft until the owner approves. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 of version 1 carry over unchanged.

actions_now: Version 1 stays approved and is not edited; I write version 2 that suspends criterion 3 and ask the owner whether email is dropped or moved to its own line. The implementer builds the other criteria; criterion 3 is not built until the owner decides. The version 1 text itself is not restated here, so only the changed criterion is shown.

specs.title: Settings kept across devices
sources: Owner request: user settings (theme and language) kept across devices
in_scope: Theme and language settings saved for a user
Saved settings applied on each device where the user signs in
non_goals: Settings other than theme and language
Changes to the look of the settings page

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user sets the theme to dark on one device, when the user signs in on another device, then that device shows the dark theme.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions for the same user.

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user sets the language, when the user signs in on another device, then that device shows that language.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions; the language list as decided in open question 1.

criteria.text: Given a user has saved no preference, when the user signs in, then the defaults decided in open question 2 apply.
criteria.check: Test of a new account; defaults as decided in open question 2.

criteria.text: Given a theme or language value the product does not offer, when a save is attempted, then the save is refused and the stored setting is unchanged.
criteria.check: Negative API test with an unsupported value.

criteria.text: Given two devices change the same setting at about the same time, when both saves complete, then the result follows the rule decided in open question 3.
criteria.check: Concurrency test per the rule decided in open question 3.

open_questions.question: Which languages are offered and which theme options exist?

options.changes: Criteria 2 and 4 take that list.

options.option: Any language the app already supports
options.changes: The list is taken from the app's translations.

open_questions.question: What are the default theme and language for a new user?

options.option: Light theme and the product's default language
options.changes: Criterion 3 states those values.

options.option: Taken from the browser or device on first sign-in
options.changes: Criterion 3 adds the detection rule.

open_questions.question: When two devices change the same setting, which change wins?

options.changes: Criterion 5 is decided by time.

options.option: The change from the current device
options.changes: Criterion 5 is decided by the device.

open_questions.question: What happens to saved settings when an account is deleted?

options.changes: Adds a deletion criterion; personal data removed.
Adds the period and its deletion rule.

actions_now: Write the draft spec on the behaviour only; the request names a table, but the table is the architect's decision, so the spec does not name it. The languages, defaults, conflict rule and account-deletion rule go to the owner as open questions, and criteria 2 to 5 wait for them while criterion 1 may proceed.

specs.title: CSV export
sources: CSV export version 2, approved (dl-015)
QA report: the spec does not say what happens above 100,000 rows; the current code times out
in_scope: Behaviour of the export when it would exceed 100,000 rows (criterion 5 only; the rest carries over from version 2)
non_goals: Changing the export content or columns

criteria.text: Given an export that would have more than 100,000 rows, when the user requests it, then the behaviour decided in open question 1 happens and no timeout is shown.
criteria.check: Integration test with a fixture of 100,001 rows; expected result as decided in open question 1.

open_questions.question: What should happen to an export above 100,000 rows?

options.option: Refuse, with a message that gives the limit and asks the user to narrow the date range
options.changes: No file is produced; criterion 5 is a clear error.

options.option: Prepare the file in the background and give a download link when it is ready
options.changes: Needs a link page or notification; criterion 5 names them.
Criterion 5 names the file count and file names.

open_questions.question: Should the 100,000-row limit itself stay as it is?

options.changes: Criterion 5 uses 100,000.
Criterion 5 uses the new value.

versions: 3 (2026-11-27): adds the row-limit behaviour as criterion 5 after the QA report; draft until the owner approves. Criteria 1 to 4 carry over from version 2 unchanged.

actions_now: Version 2 is approved and not edited; I write version 3 with criterion 5 and ask the owner in chat, since the owner is present, which behaviour applies above 100,000 rows. I do not choose the behaviour; until the owner answers, the over-limit case stays a known gap and the spec does not claim it is fixed. Only the new criterion is shown; criteria 1 to 4 carry over from version 2.

specs.title: Reports CSV export
sources: Owner request: let users export reports as CSV
Current reports page: table with columns Date, Region, Orders and Revenue; a date range filter
in_scope: Exporting the reports table as a CSV file from the reports page
non_goals: Exports of other pages
Changes to the table layout or columns on the page

criteria.text: Given the reports page shows a table, when the user exports, then the first row of the file holds the column names Date, Region, Orders and Revenue, in that order.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the header row of the file.

criteria.text: Given the table has data rows, when the user exports, then the file has one row per data row with the values shown on the page.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the file with a fixture table.

criteria.text: Given a date range filter is set, when the user exports, then the file contains the rows as decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test for the case decided in open question 1.

criteria.text: Given the filter matches no rows, when the user exports, then the file is as decided in open question 2.
criteria.check: Integration test of an empty filter result.

criteria.text: Given the export cannot be produced, when the user requests it, then an error is shown and no partial file is downloaded.
criteria.check: Negative test with a forced failure during export.

open_questions.question: Does the export follow the date range filter on screen, or always export all data?

options.changes: Criterion 3 exports only the filtered rows.
Criterion 3 exports every row regardless of the filter.

open_questions.question: What does an export with no rows contain?

options.changes: Criterion 4 is a header-only file.
Criterion 4 becomes a message.

actions_now: Write the draft spec from the request and the current page; whether the export follows the date filter and what an empty export holds are not in the request, so they go to the owner as open questions with criteria 3 and 4 blocked. Criteria 1, 2 and 5 may proceed.

No spec is written: the request already has numbered Given/when/then criteria, each with a check, so it is not a spec request. Pass it on to the architect and implementer as it stands; if they report a gap in intent, that report comes back as a spec question.

specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Team lead request, passed on by the owner: show each user when their colleagues were last online
in_scope: Showing a colleague's last-online time to a user, as decided in open question 1
non_goals: Real-time presence or online status
Changes to how activity is recorded

criteria.text: Given user A and a colleague B, when A views B, then B's last-online time is shown only to the people decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with users in and out of the group decided in open question 1.

criteria.text: Given B has chosen to hide the last-online time, when A views B, then A sees no time for B.
criteria.check: Integration test; applies only if open question 2 allows hiding.

criteria.text: Given a last-online record older than the period decided in open question 3, when the retention job runs, then the record is deleted.
criteria.check: Test with a mocked clock and an aged record.

open_questions.question: Who may see a colleague's last-online time, and who counts as a colleague?

options.changes: Criterion 1 is open to all users.
Criterion 1 needs a team definition.
Criterion 1 needs a project link.

open_questions.question: Can a user hide their own last-online time?

options.changes: Criterion 2 applies.
Criterion 2 is removed.

options.option: Yes, with a stated effect on what they can see
options.changes: Criterion 2 states the effect.

open_questions.question: How long is the last-online record kept?

options.changes: Criterion 3 states the number.
Criterion 3 becomes a deletion-with-account rule.

actions_now: Write the draft spec but do not choose who sees the time, whether it can be hidden, or how long it is kept: these are privacy decisions about people and belong to the owner. All three criteria are blocked until the owner answers; the spec is escalated to the owner now.

specs.title: Report export with all columns
sources: Owner request: exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile
Decision dl-009: personal emails never leave the system in any export
Report has a Customer email column
in_scope: Every non-email column of the report appears in exports, with the values shown on screen
non_goals: Changing what the on-screen report shows
Any export of personal email addresses, which dl-009 forbids

criteria.text: Given a report with its columns, when the user exports it, then every column except Customer email is present with the values shown on screen.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the header and values of the file with a fixture report.

criteria.text: Given any export, when it is generated, then no personal email address appears in any cell or in the file name.
criteria.check: Test that scans export output from a fixture containing emails, per dl-009.

criteria.text: Given the Customer email column, when the export is generated, then the treatment is the one the owner decides in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test for the option the owner chooses.

open_questions.question: How does finance reconcile without emails, given dl-009 forbids emails in any export?

options.option: Add a customer ID column in place of the email
options.changes: Criterion 3 becomes an ID column; dl-009 is unchanged.

options.option: Omit the email column and state the omission in the export
options.changes: Criterion 3 becomes a stated omission.

options.option: Owner revises dl-009 to allow emails in finance exports
options.changes: Criterion 2 is reversed for finance exports; only the owner can record that change.

open_questions.waiting_for: Owner (a recorded decision conflicts with the request)

actions_now: The request contradicts recorded decision dl-009, so this is escalated rather than resolved: the product role does not pick between the request and dl-009. Criteria 1 and 2 are not in conflict and may go ahead; criterion 3 waits for the owner, who alone can revise dl-009.

specs.title: Dark mode for the app
sources: Owner request: dark mode on the settings page as a toggle that applies to the whole app
App surfaces: email templates and printable invoice view
in_scope: The app's screens switch between light and dark with the toggle on the settings page
non_goals: Email templates and the printable invoice view, unless open question 1 puts them in scope

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user turns the dark mode toggle on, then every main app screen shows dark colours.
criteria.check: UI test of each main screen in both toggle states.

criteria.text: Given the toggle is on, when the user moves to another page, then the page is still dark.
criteria.check: Navigation test across pages.

criteria.text: Given the toggle is off, when any page is shown, then the existing light colours are shown.
criteria.check: Visual regression test of the light theme.

criteria.text: Given the email templates, when an email is sent, then the colours are as decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Test of a rendered email per the decision.

criteria.text: Given the printable invoice view, when the user prints it, then the output is as decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Print preview test per the decision.

criteria.text: Given the setting is saved, when the user opens the app on another device, then the theme is as decided in open question 2.
criteria.check: Integration test with two sessions per the decision.

open_questions.question: Do the email templates and the printable invoice view follow the toggle?

options.changes: Criteria 4 and 5 apply the dark colours.
Criteria 4 and 5 state the light output stays.

options.option: Only the invoice view follows it
options.changes: Criterion 4 is removed; criterion 5 applies.

open_questions.question: Is the setting stored per user or per device?

options.changes: Criterion 6 applies across devices.
Criterion 6 is removed; the setting is local.

actions_now: Write the draft spec on the literal scope, and ask the owner whether the email templates, the printable invoice view and the per-user or per-device setting are included, since the request does not say; the product role does not decide them. Criteria 1 to 3 may proceed; 4 to 6 wait for the answers.

No spec is written: this is a bug with a known cause and the expected behaviour is stated (the page as it is for users with an avatar, minus the image). Pass it to the implementer, with the check: a profile for a user with no avatar renders without error and without an image.

specs.title: Dashboard load time
sources: Owner request: make the dashboard faster
Dashboard views: Overview, Sales, Inventory
in_scope: Load time of the Overview, Sales and Inventory views
non_goals: Changes to the figures each view shows
New dashboard features

criteria.text: Given the Overview view at the data volume decided in open question 2, when a user opens it, then it is fully shown within the target decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Timed test on the reference data set, repeated runs, result compared with the target.

criteria.text: Given the Sales view at the data volume decided in open question 2, when a user opens it, then it is fully shown within the target decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Timed test as for criterion 1.

criteria.text: Given the Inventory view at the data volume decided in open question 2, when a user opens it, then it is fully shown within the target decided in open question 1.
criteria.check: Timed test as for criterion 1.

criteria.text: Given any view, when its figures load after the change, then the figures shown are the same as before the change.
criteria.check: Comparison test of figures before and after on the same data.

open_questions.question: What is the target: one time for all three views, or one per view, and is it total load time or time until the first figure appears?

options.option: One target for all views, total load time
options.changes: Criteria 1 to 3 share one number.
Each criterion carries its own number.
The measure in criteria 1 to 3 changes.

open_questions.question: Which data volume and conditions are the reference for measuring?

options.option: Current production volume at a stated date
options.changes: The reference data set is a copy of that volume.
The reference data set is defined in the spec.

actions_now: Write the draft spec with a measurable property for each view, but leave the numbers, the measure and the reference data to the owner; the request gives no threshold, so criteria 1 to 3 are blocked. Criterion 4, that the figures do not change, may proceed.
